greek: Προσθέμενος δὲ Αβρααμ ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, ᾗ ὄνομα Χεττουρα.
hint: Abraham takes another wife, Keturah.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyōsep*, *and he added*, with *and took* after it. The Greek keeps the Hebrew's idiom: the participle of προστίθημι, *to put to*, and then *took*.
The name is the Hebrew Qĕṭûrâ; the Greek declines it as a first-declension feminine.

reading: [[having put to|having put to, having handed over / delivered, having given / bestowed, having imposed further, having attributed / imputed to, having added, having made additions / augmented, having joined, having associated oneself to, having been well-inclined, having come in / submitted, having given one's assent / agreed to, having deposited, having taken to one as a friend / ally / won over, having added to oneself / gained, having brought upon oneself, having vented|προστίθημι]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[took|took, received, took hold of / grasped / seized, caught, took by violence / seized / carried off as prize / booty, attacked, seized / possessed, occupied / possessed, caught / came upon / overtook, caught / found / came upon, caught / found out / detected, bound, took / kept, assumed, apprehended by the senses, seized with the mind / apprehended / comprehended, understood, took in hand / undertook, had given one / got / gained / won, received in marriage, accepted, demanded, conceived, received as produce / profit, purchased, admitted of|λαμβάνω]] [[woman|woman, mistress / lady, wife / spouse, mortal woman|γυνή]], to whom [[a name|a name, name / fame, a mere name, a false name / pretence / pretext, a phrase / expression, a saying / speech, a noun|ὄνομα]] [[name:Χεττουρα]].

names.gloss: (Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")
(Χεττουρα, from Hebrew Qĕṭûrâ, usually connected with qĕṭōret, "incense")

greek: ἔτεκεν δὲ αὐτῷ τὸν Ζεμραν καὶ τὸν Ιεξαν καὶ τὸν Μαδαν καὶ τὸν Μαδιαμ καὶ τὸν Ιεσβοκ καὶ τὸν Σωυε.
hint: Keturah bears Abraham six sons, from Zimran to Shuah.

notes.text: The article before each name is not printed.
[[flag]] The Berlin papyrus, 911, has Ζεμραν; the first hand of Codex Alexandrinus reads Ζεβραν, its corrector Ζεμβραν.

reading: [[brought into the world|brought into the world, begot, brought forth, bore young / bred, laid eggs, bore / produced, generated / produced|τίκτω]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], to him the [[name:Ζεμραν]] and the [[name:Ιεξαν]] and the [[name:Μαδαν]] and the [[name:Μαδιαμ]] and the [[name:Ιεσβοκ]] and the [[name:Σωυε]].

names.gloss: (Ζεμραν, from Hebrew Zimrān, of uncertain meaning)
(Ιεξαν, from Hebrew Yoqšān, of uncertain meaning)
(Μαδαν, from Hebrew Mĕdān, of uncertain meaning)
(Μαδιαμ, from Hebrew Midyān, of uncertain meaning)
(Ιεσβοκ, from Hebrew Yišbāq, of uncertain meaning)
(Σωυε, from Hebrew Šûaḥ, usually connected with šûaḥ, "to sink down")

greek: Ιεξαν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαβα καὶ τὸν Θαιμαν καὶ τὸν Δαιδαν· υἱοὶ δὲ Δαιδαν ἐγένοντο Ραγουηλ καὶ Ναβδεηλ καὶ Ασσουριιμ καὶ Λατουσιιμ καὶ Λοωμιμ.
hint: Jokshan's sons Sheba, Teman and Dedan, and Dedan's five sons.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew of this verse, which has Sheba and Dedan alone.
[[flag]] Not in the Hebrew, whose sons of Dedan are the Asshurim, the Letushim and the Leummim.
Peoples of the Hebrew plural in -îm, indeclinable here, and plural and masculine from the people, as the Λουδιιμ of 10:13.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Σαβαν, and ασουριμ.

reading: [[name:Ιεξαν]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[begot|begot / engendered, brought forth, produced|γεννάω]] the [[name:Σαβα]] and the [[name:Θαιμαν]] and the [[name:Δαιδαν]]; sons [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], of [[name:Δαιδαν]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[name:Ραγουηλ]] and [[name:Ναβδεηλ]] and [[name:Ασσουριιμ]] and [[name:Λατουσιιμ]] and [[name:Λοωμιμ]].

names.gloss: (Σαβα, from Hebrew Šĕbāʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Θαιμαν, from Hebrew Têmān, "south" or "the south country")
(Δαιδαν, from Hebrew Dĕdān, of uncertain meaning)
(Ραγουηλ, from Hebrew Rĕʿûʾēl, "friend of God")
(Ναβδεηλ, for Hebrew ʿAbdĕʾēl, "servant of God", as at 25:13)
(Ασσουριιμ, from Hebrew ʾAššûrim, a people of the Hebrew plural in -îm)
(Λατουσιιμ, from Hebrew Lĕṭûšim, a people of the Hebrew plural in -îm)
(Λοωμιμ, from Hebrew Lĕʾummim, a people of the Hebrew plural in -îm, connected with lĕʾōm, "people")

greek: υἱοὶ δὲ Μαδιαμ· Γαιφα καὶ Αφερ καὶ Ενωχ καὶ Αβιρα καὶ Ελραγα. πάντες οὗτοι ἦσαν υἱοὶ Χεττουρας.
hint: Midian's five sons; all these are counted sons of Keturah.

notes.text: ἦν of a standing state, the formula of GEN 1:2 in full, in the plural.
[[flag]] Rahlfs prints Γαιφα, with a few witnesses; Codex Alexandrinus reads Γεφαρ, and θεργαμα for Ελραγα, and puts οὗτοι πάντες the other way round.

reading: sons [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], of [[name:Μαδιαμ]]; [[name:Γαιφα]] and [[name:Αφερ]] and [[name:Ενωχ]] and [[name:Αβιρα]] and [[name:Ελραγα]]. [[all|all / the whole, all, nothing but, every, everyone, every single, the whole, quite, full, of all kinds|πᾶς]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, sons of [[name:Χεττουρας]].

names.gloss: (Γαιφα, for Hebrew ʿÊpâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Αφερ, from Hebrew ʿĒper, usually connected with ʿōper, "fawn")
(Ενωχ, from Hebrew Ḥănôk, usually connected with ḥānak, "to dedicate")
(Αβιρα, for Hebrew ʾĂbîdāʿ, "my father knows")
(Ελραγα, for Hebrew ʾEldāʿâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: Ἔδωκεν δὲ Αβρααμ πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ Ισαακ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ,
hint: Abraham gives all he has to Isaac.

notes.text: ὑπάρχω, the chain of GEN 12:5.

reading: [[gave|gave, granted, provided, offered to the gods, tendered, gave over / delivered up, pardoned, forgave, remitted, granted / allowed / brought about that, gave oneself up / devoted oneself|δίδωμι]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[all|all / the whole, all, nothing but, every, everyone, every single, the whole, quite, full, of all kinds, all things, everything|πᾶς]] [[the existing circumstances|the existing circumstances / present advantages, the what belongs to one / one's possessions / means|ὑπάρχω]] of him to [[name:Ισαακ]] to the son of him,

names.gloss: (Ισαακ, from Hebrew Yiṣḥāq, "he laughs")

greek: καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν παλλακῶν αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν Αβρααμ δόματα καὶ ἐξαπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ Ισαακ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ ἔτι ζῶντος αὐτοῦ πρὸς ἀνατολὰς εἰς γῆν ἀνατολῶν.
hint: The concubines' sons get gifts and are sent east, away from Isaac, while Abraham still lives.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ's δόμα is *gift*, then *payment*.
The genitive absolute, `living`, as καθημένου at 18:1.
παλλακή, filed under παλλακίς, the chain of GEN 22:24.

greek: Ταῦτα δὲ τὰ ἔτη ἡμερῶν ζωῆς Αβρααμ, ὅσα ἔζησεν· ἑκατὸν ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε ἔτη.
hint: Abraham's life: a hundred and seventy-five years.

notes.text: Three genitives in a row, as the Hebrew *šĕnê ḥayyê ʾabrāhām*, *the years of the life of Abraham*, with *days* added.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], the years [[of days|of days, of states / times of life|ἡμέρα]] [[of the life|of the life / existence, of the living, of the means of life / substance, of a way of life|ζωή]] of [[name:Αβρααμ]], [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] [[lived|lived, lived off or on, was in full life and strength / fresh / strong|ζάω]]; hundred seventy five years.

greek: καὶ ἐκλιπὼν ἀπέθανεν Αβρααμ ἐν γήρει καλῷ πρεσβύτης καὶ πλήρης ἡμερῶν καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
hint: Abraham dies in a good old age, full of days, and is added to his people.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyēʾāsep ʾel-ʿammāyw*, *and he was gathered to his peoples*. The Greek has προστίθημι, *to put to*, in the passive, and the people in the singular.
ἐκλείπω, the chain of GEN 8:13, in the aorist participle: the Hebrew is *wayyigwaʿ*, *and he expired*.
πρεσβύτης is *= πρέσβυς I*, whose first sense is *an old man*; πλήρης's first sense is untranslated in Middle Liddell, and its first English is *filled*.

greek: καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν Ισαακ καὶ Ισμαηλ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ σπήλαιον τὸ διπλοῦν εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν Εφρων τοῦ Σααρ τοῦ Χετταίου, ὅ ἐστιν ἀπέναντι Μαμβρη,
hint: Isaac and Ishmael bury Abraham in the double cave, in Ephron's field facing Mamre.

notes.text: σπήλαιον and διπλοῦς, the chains of GEN 23:9.
The article with the genitive, *the one of Saar*, as at 23:8; the article before the people's name is not printed.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts δύο before it; the Berlin papyrus, 911, does not.

names.gloss: (Ισμαηλ, from Hebrew Yišmāʿēʾl, "God hears")
(Εφρων, from Hebrew ʿEprôn, of uncertain meaning)
(Σααρ, from Hebrew Ṣōḥar, of uncertain meaning)
(Χετταῖος, the man of Χετ, Heth; Hebrew Ḥittî)
(Μαμβρη, from Hebrew Mamrēʾ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: τὸν ἀγρὸν καὶ τὸ σπήλαιον, ὃ ἐκτήσατο Αβρααμ παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Χετ, ἐκεῖ ἔθαψαν Αβρααμ καὶ Σαρραν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ.
hint: The field and cave Abraham bought from the sons of Heth hold both Abraham and Sarah.

notes.text: κτάομαι is first *to procure for oneself, to get, gain, acquire*.

reading: [[the field|the field, the fields / lands, the farm, the country|ἀγρός]] and [[the grotto|the grotto / cave / cavern|σπήλαιον]], which [[procured for himself|procured for himself / got / gained / acquired, won, brought upon himself / incurred, procured for another, made|κτάομαι]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] of the sons of [[name:Χετ]], [[there|there, in that place, in another world, thither|ἐκεῖ]] [[paid the last dues to a corpse|paid the last dues to a corpse / honoured with funeral rites, buried / interred|θάπτω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[name:Σαρραν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress / lady, the wife / spouse, the mortal woman|γυνή]] of him.

names.gloss: (Χετ, from Hebrew Ḥēt, of uncertain meaning)
(Σαρρα, from Hebrew Śārâ, "princess")

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν Αβρααμ εὐλόγησεν ὁ θεὸς Ισαακ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ· καὶ κατῴκησεν Ισαακ παρὰ τὸ φρέαρ τῆς ὁράσεως.
hint: After Abraham's death God blesses Isaac, who settles by the Well of the Vision.

notes.text: The article before the infinitive is not printed; Αβρααμ is its accusative subject.
As at 24:62, and the name of 16:14.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts τόν before the first Ισαακ; the Berlin papyrus, 911, does not.

reading: [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit / quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[the dying off|the dying off / dying, the being ready to die, the being put to death / slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[spoke well of|spoke well of / praised / honoured, blessed|εὐλογέω]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[name:Ισαακ]] the son of him; and [[dwelt in as a katoikos (κάτοικος)|dwelt in as a katoikos (κάτοικος), settled in / colonised, inhabited, settled / dwelt, lay / was situate|κατοικέω]] [[name:Ισαακ]] [[to the side of|to the side of, motion alongside of, to, beside / near / by, passing by, beyond, contrary to / against, beside / except, on account of / because of / by means of, along the whole course of / during|παρά + accusative]] [[the well|the well, the tank / cistern / reservoir, the oil jar|φρέαρ]] [[of the seeing|of the seeing / act of sight, of the vision|ὅρασις]].

greek: Αὗται δὲ αἱ γενέσεις Ισμαηλ τοῦ υἱοῦ Αβρααμ, ὃν ἔτεκεν Αγαρ ἡ παιδίσκη Σαρρας τῷ Αβρααμ,
hint: The generations of Ishmael, son of Abraham by Hagar, Sarah's maid.

notes.text: γένεσις, the chain of GEN 2:4, in the plural, as at 6:9.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[the origins|the origins / sources / productive causes, the beginnings, the manners of birth, the races / descents, the productions / generations, the creations / created things, the races / kinds / families, the generations / ages|γένεσις]] of [[name:Ισμαηλ]] of the son of [[name:Αβρααμ]], whom [[brought into the world|brought into the world, begot, brought forth, bore young / bred, laid eggs, bore / produced, generated / produced|τίκτω]] [[name:Αγαρ]] [[the young girl|the young girl / maiden, the young slave / courtesan|παιδίσκη]] of [[name:Σαρρας]] to the [[name:Αβρααμ]],

names.gloss: (Αγαρ, from Hebrew Hāgār, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν υἱῶν Ισμαηλ κατʼ ὄνομα τῶν γενεῶν αὐτοῦ· πρωτότοκος Ισμαηλ Ναβαιωθ καὶ Κηδαρ καὶ Ναβδεηλ καὶ Μασσαμ
hint: The names of Ishmael's sons, starting with Nebaioth the firstborn.

notes.text: γενεά is first *race, stock, family*, then *a race, generation*.
πρωτότοκος, one sense, *first-born*: plain text, as at 10:15.

reading: and [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the names|the names, the names / fames, the mere names, the false names / pretences / pretexts, the phrases / expressions, the sayings / speeches, the nouns|ὄνομα]] of the sons of [[name:Ισμαηλ]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[a name|a name, name / fame, a mere name, a false name / pretence / pretext, a phrase / expression, a saying / speech, a noun|ὄνομα]] [[of the races|of the races / stocks / families, of the breeds, of the tribes / nations, of the races / generations, of the offspring, of the birth-places, of the eyries, of the ages / times of life, of the times of birth|γενεά]] of him; first-born of [[name:Ισμαηλ]] [[name:Ναβαιωθ]] and [[name:Κηδαρ]] and [[name:Ναβδεηλ]] and [[name:Μασσαμ]]

names.gloss: (Ναβαιωθ, from Hebrew Nĕbāyôt, of uncertain meaning)
(Κηδαρ, from Hebrew Qēdār, usually connected with qādar, "to be dark")
(Μασσαμ, for Hebrew Mibśām, usually connected with bōśem, "balsam, spice")

greek: καὶ Μασμα καὶ Ιδουμα καὶ Μασση
hint: Three more of Ishmael's sons: Mishma, Dumah and Massa.

notes.text: Rahlfs prints no punctuation at the end of the verse.

reading: and [[name:Μασμα]] and [[name:Ιδουμα]] and [[name:Μασση]]

names.gloss: (Μασμα, from Hebrew Mišmāʿ, usually connected with šāmaʿ, "to hear")
(Ιδουμα, for Hebrew Dûmâ, usually connected with dāmam, "to be silent")
(Μασση, from Hebrew Maśśāʾ, usually connected with nāśāʾ, "to lift, bear")

greek: καὶ Χοδδαδ καὶ Θαιμαν καὶ Ιετουρ καὶ Ναφες καὶ Κεδμα.
hint: The last five sons of Ishmael, from Hadad to Kedemah.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Χοδδαν.

reading: and [[name:Χοδδαδ]] and [[name:Θαιμαν]] and [[name:Ιετουρ]] and [[name:Ναφες]] and [[name:Κεδμα]].

names.gloss: (Χοδδαδ, for Hebrew Ḥădad, the name of a storm-god)
(Ιετουρ, from Hebrew Yĕṭûr, of uncertain meaning)
(Ναφες, from Hebrew Nāpîš, usually connected with nepeš, "breath, soul")
(Κεδμα, from Hebrew Qēdĕmâ, usually connected with qedem, "east")

greek: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ισμαηλ καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα αὐτῶν ἐν ταῖς σκηναῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἐπαύλεσιν αὐτῶν· δώδεκα ἄρχοντες κατὰ ἔθνη αὐτῶν.
hint: Ishmael's sons: twelve rulers of nations, named by their tents and folds.

notes.text: ἔπαυλις, one sense, *a fold*, with ἐν.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus has the singular, ἔθνος.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] are the sons of [[name:Ισμαηλ]] and [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the names|the names, the names / fames, the mere names, the false names / pretences / pretexts, the phrases / expressions, the sayings / speeches, the nouns|ὄνομα]] of them [[in the covered places|within, inside of, and by means of the covered places / tents, the camps, the dwelling-places / houses / temples, the wooden stages, the stage-effects / unrealities, the tented covers / tilts of a wagon, the bed-testers, the entertainments given in tents / banquets|ἐν; σκηνή]] of them and [[in the folds|within, inside of, and by means of the folds|ἐν; ἔπαυλις]] of them; twelve [[the rulers|the rulers / commanders / chiefs / captains, the chief magistrates at Athens|ἄρχων]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[numbers of people accustomed to live together|numbers of people accustomed to live together / companies / bodies of men, hosts, swarms / flocks, nations / peoples, nations / gentiles, special classes, castes / tribes, sexes|ἔθνος]] of them.

greek: καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ἔτη τῆς ζωῆς Ισμαηλ· ἑκατὸν τριάκοντα ἑπτὰ ἔτη· καὶ ἐκλιπὼν ἀπέθανεν καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τὸ γένος αὐτοῦ.
hint: Ishmael dies at a hundred and thirty-seven and is added to his race.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyēʾāsep ʾel-ʿammāyw*, *and he was gathered to his peoples*, as at 25:8. The Greek has *to the race of him*.

notes.text: LSJ files ἕψεμα as the late form of ἕψημα, *anything boiled*, then *vegetables fit for kitchen use*.
ἐκλείπω, the chain of GEN 8:13: the Hebrew is *ʿāyēp*, *faint*.

reading: [[boiled|boiled / seethed, smelted / refined, cherished|ἕψω]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[anything boiled|anything boiled, vegetables for kitchen use|ἕψεμα]]; [[came|came / went, came / went back / returned|ἔρχομαι]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Ησαυ]] [[out of|out of, out of / forth from, from, outside of / beyond, on, upon, for, after, in or by, by the hand of, of, in consequence, by means of, according to|ἐκ]] [[of the plain|of the plain / flat, of the plain flat open country|πεδίον]] [[leaving out|leaving out / omitting / passing over, forsaking / deserting / abandoning, suffering an eclipse, dying, leaving off / ceasing / stopping, failing / being wanting|ἐκλείπω]],

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ησαυ τῷ Ιακωβ Γεῦσόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἑψέματος τοῦ πυρροῦ τούτου, ὅτι ἐκλείπω. διὰ τοῦτο ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Εδωμ.
hint: Fainting, Esau asks for the red stew, and from it is named Edom.

notes.text: γεύω in the active, one sense, *to give a taste of*: plain text; its middle senses, *to taste of*, belong to the other voice.
πυρρός is first *flame-coloured, yellowish-red*; the Hebrew ʾādōm is heard in the name Ἐδωμ.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone adds ἐγώ.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said / spoke, said / declared, said something of, called by name, told, boasted of / told of, recited|λέγω]] [[name:Ησαυ]] to the [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[give a taste of|give a taste of, taste of, taste / feel, taste the sweets of, have experience of|γεύω]] me [[from|from, away from, away from / far from / apart from, alien from, of, from / after, sprung from, in descent from, born of, from or of, from or by, because of, by reason of, moved by / for, what is one's own|ἀπό]] [[of the anything boiled|of the anything boiled, of the vegetables for kitchen use|ἕψεμα]] [[of the flame-coloured|of the flame-coloured / yellowish-red, of the red-haired, of the red / tawny, of the red with blushes|πυρρός]] [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]], [[that|that, for that / because / seeing that / inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[I leave out|I leave out / omit / pass over, I forsake / desert / abandon, I suffer an eclipse, I die, I leave off / cease / stop, I fail / am wanting|ἐκλείπω]]. [[through|through, throughout / over, during, by aid of / by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[was called|was called / summoned, was called to a repast / invited, was called on / invoked, was cited / summoned, was called by name / called / named|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the name / fame, the mere name, the false name / pretence / pretext, the phrase / expression, the saying / speech, the noun|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Εδωμ]].

names.gloss: (Εδωμ, from Hebrew ʾĔdôm, which the Hebrew of 25:30 hears in ʾādōm, "red")

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιακωβ τῷ Ησαυ Ἀπόδου μοι σήμερον τὰ πρωτοτόκιά σου ἐμοί.
hint: Jacob asks Esau to sell him his birthright that day.

notes.text: The middle of ἀποδίδωμι, *to give away of one's own will, to sell*.
The pronoun twice over, *of you* and *to me*, as the Hebrew *lî*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said / spoke, said / declared, said something of, called by name, told, boasted of / told of, recited|λέγω]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] to the [[name:Ησαυ]] [[give away of your own will|give away of your own will / sell, give up / back / restore / return, render what is due / pay, return / render / yield, yield fruit, suffer / allow, deliver over / give up, increase, farm out|ἀποδίδωμι]] to me to-day [[the rights of the first-born|the rights of the first-born / birthright|πρωτοτόκια]] of you to me.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ησαυ Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ πορεύομαι τελευτᾶν, καὶ ἵνα τί μοι ταῦτα τὰ πρωτοτόκια;
hint: Esau, about to die, asks what use a birthright is to him.

notes.text: τελευτάω is first *to complete, finish, accomplish*; *to end life, to die* is within its first sense.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said / spoke, said / declared, said something of, called by name, told, boasted of / told of, recited|λέγω]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Ησαυ]] [[lo|lo / behold / see there, there, well / as you please, oh yes|ἰδού]] I [[I am driven|I am driven / carried, I go / walk / march, I go across / pass, I enter, I go over / traverse, I live|πορεύομαι]] [[to complete|to complete / finish / accomplish, to fulfil an oath / promise, to bring about, to bring to an end, to end life / die, to make an end of, to come to an end, to end / issue in|τελευτάω]], and [[that|in order that, that he might, that not|ἵνα]] what to me [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the rights of the first-born|the rights of the first-born / birthright|πρωτοτόκια]]?

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ιακωβ Ὄμοσόν μοι σήμερον. καὶ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ· ἀπέδοτο δὲ Ησαυ τὰ πρωτοτόκια τῷ Ιακωβ.
hint: Esau swears to Jacob and sells him the birthright.

notes.text: The middle of ἀποδίδωμι, as at 25:31.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said / spoke, said / declared, said something of, called by name, told, boasted of / told of, recited|λέγω]] to him [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[swear|swear, swear that one will, swear to / affirm / confirm by oath, swear by|ὄμνυμι]] to me to-day. and [[swore|swore, swore that one would, swore to / affirmed / confirmed by oath, swore by|ὄμνυμι]] to him; [[gave away of his own will|gave away of his own will / sold, gave up / back / restored / returned, rendered what is due / paid, returned / rendered / yielded, yielded fruit, suffered / allowed, delivered over / gave up, increased, farmed out|ἀποδίδωμι]] [[but|but, while / whereas / on the other hand, then / yet, at, I say / now / so then|δέ]], [[name:Ησαυ]] [[the rights of the first-born|the rights of the first-born / birthright|πρωτοτόκια]] to the [[name:Ιακωβ]].

greek: Ιακωβ δὲ ἔδωκεν τῷ Ησαυ ἄρτον καὶ ἕψεμα φακοῦ, καὶ ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔπιεν καὶ ἀναστὰς ᾤχετο· καὶ ἐφαύλισεν Ησαυ τὰ πρωτοτόκια.
hint: Esau eats Jacob's bread and lentils, rises, goes, and holds the birthright cheap.

notes.text: οἴχομαι, the chain of GEN 12:4: the imperfect stands for a completed departure.
φαυλίζω, one sense, *to hold cheap, to depreciate, disparage*.
